chapter_theme: Punnakku Siddhar's twenty short stanzas to 'Jnanam, mother' (ஞானம்மா): true knowledge is a priceless gem found by passing beyond ignorance, the life sits in the body like the chick in the egg, and the seeker must give up sleep, see waking as a dream and so make Death bow. Against this he sets those who take samsara for real, the untaught swamis who roam for property, the smearing, talk, puja and hand-waving that are only a target for mockery, the drums and wailing of a funeral that never counts its own days, and a body that is borrowed, wind-filled, filthy and saltless, a false nest the five senses built to rule.
structure_note: Each stanza is three short lines with the refrain ஞானம்மா in the third, the second half of a line turning on 'Jnanam, mother' to deliver the point. 2247 to 2255 teach (refuge, the gem, the chick, the remainder of past births, the waking seeker); 2256 to 2261 mock (swamis, rites, funerals, borrowed things, talkers); 2262 to 2266 return to the guru, the light and the false body. From 2261 the parsed text carries a heading that looks like a lost first line (see source_issues).

2247.reading: Crying 'refuge, refuge', I leapt and begged to see the holy feet of the goddess Manonmani, Jnanam, mother.
2247.nuance: The opening is a plea for refuge to Manonmani, the Shakti beyond mind; ஞானம்மா, the refrain, addresses knowledge itself as a mother, so the goddess and jnana are run together from the first stanza.

2248.reading: If one passes beyond ignorance, drives the understanding hard and finds true knowledge, Jnanam, mother, it is a gem without price.
2248.nuance: அறிவு (understanding) is the instrument and மெய்ஞ்ஞானம் the find; the verse makes knowledge something one drives toward, not something given.

2249.reading: As a whole chick lies within the egg, so, Jnanam, mother, the life itself stands within the body that is a shirt.
2249.nuance: Two images of the body in one line: the egg-shell, inside which something complete is already formed, and the சட்டை, a shirt or a snake's slough that is put off. The life is whole before it hatches; the body is only its covering.

2250.reading: When the remainder left off does not return and true knowledge is not sought, it is through the remainder once touched, Jnanam, mother, that true knowledge appears.
2250.nuance: விட்ட குறை தொட்ட குறை is a proverbial pair, taken by tradition as the unfinished practice or karma of a former birth that carries over. The stanza seems to say that knowledge arises from what was begun before, even where present seeking fails; the logic of the two negatives is unclear.

2251.reading: Not knowing their own hearts, not knowing the breath, taking household life for truth, Jnanam, mother, they toil in the sea.
2251.nuance: சரம் is the breath (svara), so not knowing the breath stands beside not knowing oneself as the double cause of drowning. சம்சாரம் is both the round of birth and, in Tamil use, family life; the sea (சாகரம்) is the traditional figure for the first.

2252.reading: One may give teaching to the willing any day; but to give teaching to the wicked, Jnanam, mother, brings ruin.
2252.nuance: இட்டர், those dear or willing, against துட்டர், the wicked. The ruin (மோசம்) may fall on the teacher, on the teaching, or on both; the stanza does not say.

2253.reading: Those who would gain release, and those who have set it first in their thought, must give up sleep, Jnanam, mother, and stay with awareness.
2253.nuance: நித்திரையும் விட்டு may be literal sleeplessness, as in the vigils of the ascetics (compare Mounachiddhar's 2241), or the giving up of the sleep of unawareness. நினைவோடு, with awareness or with remembrance, is the positive term.

2254.reading: If you look on waking as a dream, then even Yama who comes in anger, Jnanam, mother, will fall prostrate and go.
2254.nuance: நினைவு here is the waking state as against dream; to see it as a dream is to stop taking the world as solid. The claim is that this seeing undoes death: Yama bows (தெண்டநிட்டு) instead of seizing. It can also be read more plainly, that one who holds waking life lightly does not fear death.

2255.reading: Not knowing the truth by the light of the lamp of yoga, they sink, Jnanam, mother, into the pit called delusion.
2255.nuance: Yoga is a lamp: its use is to show the truth, and without it one falls into மோகம், infatuation. The pit is the dark that the lamp would have shown.

2256.reading: Becoming swamis who never learned the shastras, thinking to seek property, Jnanam, mother, crores of them wander.
2256.nuance: ஆத்தி is probably ஆஸ்தி, property; the garb is taken for gain. Unusually for the Siddhars, the charge is that these swamis have not learned the shastras: here book-learning is a minimum, not the enemy.

2257.reading: Smearing, empty talk, puja and the waving of hands are only a mark for mockery, Jnanam, mother: there is nothing in any of it.
2257.nuance: பூச்சு is the smearing of ash or sandal, கைவீச்சு the hand-gestures of ritual or of preaching. The rhyme (பூச்சு, பேச்சு, கைவீச்சு, ஏச்சு) does the arguing: outward show invites ridicule.

2258.reading: Adorning the vessel, the women with hair unbound, not knowing the reckoning, Jnanam, mother, wept in confusion.
2258.nuance: The scene is a funeral: women loosen their hair in mourning. கலம் may be the pot or bier of the dead, or the body itself as a vessel; கணக்கு, the reckoning, is perhaps the count of days or deeds that the mourners never learned.

2259.reading: Beating the drums and many people gathering, never counting their own days, Jnanam, mother, they waste away and weep.
2259.nuance: The mourners weep for another and do not count their own span: the point is not grief but the failure to draw the lesson from it.

2260.reading: The loincloth is borrowed, the gross body that was taken is borrowed, the divine mother is borrowed, Jnanam, mother; not knowing this, they wander.
2260.nuance: இரவல் (on loan) is the word that carries it: even the ascetic's loincloth and the body are lent. தேவமாதா, the divine mother, is surprising on the list; it may mean the earthly mother who bore the body, called divine, so that the parent too is lent for a time.

2261.reading: Talking like noble men, Jnanam, mother, they roam the world.
2261.nuance: The stanza has two of its three lines. The heading the parser attached to this and the following units, செத்தவரை மயானம் சேர்க்கும்வரையில் ஞானம், rhymes with உத்தமர் and is probably the lost first line: the 'jnana' that lasts only until the dead are taken to the burning ground. With it the stanza mocks graveside wisdom that fades once the body is burned.

2262.reading: Though one lives in the forest and performs golden austerities, Jnanam, mother, without a guru one cannot find and know it.
2262.nuance: கனகதவம், golden or great tapas, is granted its full worth and still found insufficient. The repetition of காட்டில் in both lines may be a copying slip or a deliberate echo.

2263.reading: The good light is the light of knowledge; the light that is no light, Jnanam, mother, is a base light.
2263.nuance: இல்லா வெளிச்சம், 'the light that is not', may be the light of the senses and the world, which is not true light and so is low; or it may be read as 'the light that is not there', the dark. The plain claim is that only the light of jnana is good.

2264.reading: Those who suffer, calling it samsara, calling it an ocean: Jnanam, mother, what use is it that they live?
2264.nuance: The stanza answers 2251: those who toiled in the sea there now only name it and complain. Calling the world an ocean is not escaping it.

2265.reading: This came shut in with wind; this is a filthy pot; this is a stinking corpse, Jnanam, mother, a saltless false nest.
2265.nuance: காத்தடைத்து, shut in with wind, makes the body a thing kept alive only by the breath held inside it. உப்பிலா, without salt, is tasteless and worthless; பொய்க்கூடு, the false nest or cage, returns in 2266.

2266.reading: The five came together seeking to rule as kings, and to move about, Jnanam, mother, they built themselves this false nest.
2266.nuance: அஞ்சுபேர், the five, are taken as the five senses, or the five elements, or the five vital airs; on any reading the body is their building and their kingdom, not the self's. தானமைத்த may also mean 'which he himself built', the Lord or maya as builder.

links.note: The Kural's bird leaves its egg or nest empty, an image of how slight the bond of body and life is; Punnakku's chick lies whole in the egg, an image of the life complete within the body-shirt. The same egg, used once for leaving and once for what is already inside.

The Kural asks whether the life lodging in a corner of the body has found no home of its own; Punnakku says the body and even the loincloth are on loan. Both make the body a lent or rented place, not the self's possession.

The Naladiyar's drummers beat three times and the dying carry the dead; Punnakku's mourners beat drums and weep without counting their own days. Both use the funeral drum to show that those who mourn are on the same road.

Both call the body a pot filled with wind and filth. Pattinathar's poet loved it and carried it about; Punnakku names it a saltless false nest, built by the five to rule, so the same pot is a confession in one and a diagnosis in the other.

Tirumular says to teach only those of ripe mind; Punnakku says teaching the willing is always fine and teaching the wicked brings ruin. The same rule of fitness, Punnakku adding the danger of breaking it.

Tirumular's formless Lord cannot be reached by anyone without the guru; Punnakku's forest-dweller of golden austerities cannot find it without a guru. Both make the guru necessary even where effort is complete.

Pattinathar lists observances, Vedas, fire rites, japa, ash and sandal and the pujas of every watch and calls all of it pretence; Punnakku compresses the list to smearing, talk, puja and hand-waving and calls it a mark for mockery.

source_issues: 2261 to 2266 carry the parsed label 'செத்தவரை மயானம் சேர்க்கும்வரையில் ஞானம்'. It rhymes with 2261's surviving line உத்தமர்போலப் பேசி and is probably 2261's lost first line, misread as a section heading and copied to the following units; 2261 has only two lines.
2262 repeats காட்டில் in its first two lines, perhaps a copying slip.
2256 ஆத்தி is probably ஆஸ்தி (property); 2260 தேவமாதா is unexpected in the list and may be corrupt.
